subtitle: The whole course in one chain: Pt100 thermometer to 3-bit code on LEDs
takeaways: One 4 V reference for bridge and ladder: ratiometric
Anti-aliasing filter removes 50 Hz before sampling
Verify in Falstad at bin centres, not at thresholds

slides.title: Five stages from sensor to code
bullets: Interference: 5 mV at 50 Hz in series with the sensor
Every stage is a circuit from an earlier chapter
slides.notes: Bridge from chapter Bridge Circuits, INA from Operational Amplifiers, low-pass from Active Filters, S&H from Sample and Hold, flash ADC from the previous chapter, LED resistor from Basics. This chapter is the worked solution of Exercise 10.1.

slides.title: Design values at a glance
bullets: Pt100, 100 … 138.5 Ω, sensor current ≈ 1 mA
Anti-aliasing 6.8 kΩ, 10 µF: f_{c} = 2.34 Hz
S&H: f_{s} = 5 Hz, 20 ms window, C_{H} = 1 µF
Flash: 8 × 1 kΩ, 7 comparators; display 10 × (LED + 330 Ω)
slides.notes: These numbers run through the whole course; keep them on screen as the reference for the next slides. The full specification table is in section The Measurement Chain.

slides.title: Stage 1: bridge, INA and gain
bullets: Bridge fed from the 4.00 V reference, balanced at 0 °C (R_{4} = 100 Ω)
Bridge output 0 … 37.18 mV; buffers keep the bridge unloaded
Difference amp G_{1} = 10, gain stage G_{2} = 1 + 97.6 k/10 k = 10.76
Keep G < 100 per stage: gain error ≈ G/A
Zero set by R_{4}, span by R_{F}: trims do not interact
slides.notes: Ratiometric: if the reference is 1 % high, bridge output and ADC thresholds are both 1 % high, the code does not change (Exercise 10.2). Trim: set 100 Ω and check 0 V, then 138.5 Ω and adjust R_F for 4.00 V.

slides.title: Stage 2: anti-aliasing low-pass
bullets: 50 Hz sampled at 5 Hz → alias at 0 Hz: a constant, invisible offset
Hum after gain 107.6 ≈ 0.52 V, about one full LSB
Residual 25 mV < ½ LSB = 250 mV; follower decouples the RC
slides.notes: For 3 bits a first-order filter is enough. For 10 bit the residual would be twelve times too large: then use 2nd or 3rd order, oversampling, or a sampling rate that is not a sub-multiple of 50 Hz (Exercise 10.3).

slides.title: Stage 3: choosing the hold capacitor

left.head: Upper limit: charging
bullets: τ = R_{on}·C_{H} = 20 Ω · 1 µF = 20 µs
Settle to ½ LSB in 2.8·τ ≪ 20 ms window
Too large C_{H}: staircase lags the input

right.head: Lower limit: droop
bullets: ΔV = I_{L}·t_{hold}/C_{H} = 0.18 mV
1 nA leakage over 180 ms hold time
Too small C_{H}: held value drifts

slides.notes: Clock 5 Hz with 10 % duty: 20 ms track, 180 ms hold. Both limits leave a wide range, 10 nF to 100 µF; choose a 1 µF film capacitor. Exercise 10.5 redoes this with R_on = 1 kΩ and 10 nA.

slides.section: Stages 4 and 5: Flash ADC, Encoder and Display
slides.title: Stages 4 and 5: flash ADC and display
bullets: Ladder 8 × 1 kΩ from 4.00 V: thresholds 0.5 … 3.5 V, 0.5 mA
C_{k} = 1 if V_{HOLD} > k·0.5 V: thermometer code, level 0 … 7
7 red LEDs as bar graph, 3 green LEDs for the binary code
330 Ω per LED from 5 V logic: about 9.8 mA in Falstad
slides.notes: Same converter as in the ADC chapter, Falstad example flash3. The full encoder equation for B0 is in section Stages 4 and 5. Exercise 10.4 extends it to four bits.

slides.title: Falstad: the complete chain

falstad.name: capstone
falstad.hint: Move Sensor R 100 → 138.5 Ω: bar fills, binary LEDs count

observe: Hover over VCOND, VAA, VHOLD: the held value updates every 200 ms
After a slider step wait ≈ 0.5 s: the low-pass needs 5τ = 340 ms
Bin-centre test points: e.g. 116.75 Ω → 1.75 V → code 011
slides.notes: Verification table in section The Complete Chain in Falstad: 6.2, 18.6, 43.5, 56.0, 81.1, 93.7 °C give codes 000, 001, 011, 100, 110, 111, with V_HOLD within 1 mV of the target.

slides.title: Falstad: the aliasing experiment

falstad.name: capstone_nofilter
falstad.hint: Sensor R = 116.75 Ω (V_{COND} = 1.75 V): code 100, not 011

observe: S&H samples V_{COND} directly; 0.52 V of 50 Hz is always hit at the same phase
Held value is a clean staircase, just 0.52 V too high: one code too high
With the filter (capstone) the same input gives the correct code 011
slides.notes: This is the worst-case phase; the offset size depends on the phase between mains and sampling clock. The point: nothing on the scope looks wrong, only the code is.

slides.title: Design recipe: sensor to digital value
steps: Fix range and resolution: full scale, N bits, LSB = V_{FS}/2^{N}
Share one reference between sensor excitation and ladder (ratiometric)
Set total gain = V_{FS}/bridge span; split into stages with G < 100
Choose f_{s}, then an anti-aliasing filter keeping hum < ½ LSB
Size C_{H} between droop and charging limits; verify at bin centres
slides.notes: This is the procedure behind the capstone task, Exercise 10.1. Students should do the paper design first and then check every stage against the Falstad model.
